posts.text: How did the US presidency get so powerful? In a country founded on democratic checks and balances, executive authority has been expanding since long before Pres. Trump took office—well beyond what the Founders intended. I’ll explain how tomorrow night in my latest @CNN special, “The Imperial Presidency,” airing Sunday @ 8pm ET/PT

On GPS, at 10am & 1pm ET Sunday on @CNN …
• This week, the US & Iran traded fire in the Strait of Hormuz, even as Washington insisted their ceasefire was still holding. Is there an endgame in sight? I’ll ask @citrinowicz, who formerly headed the Iran branch of Israel’s military intelligence
• What can you learn about America’s nearly 250 years of history by going on a road trip? I’ll ask Pulitzer-winning historian @beverlygage, who did just that for her new book, “This Land Is Your Land: A Road

Has the American president become more like a king? 
 
Pres. Trump has used executive power in unprecedented ways, but the expansion of that authority is a longer story that goes back decades. Sunday night @ 8pm ET/PT, I’ll tell that story in my latest @CNN special, “The Imperial Presidency"

Airing Sunday night @ 8pm ET/PT: my latest hour-long @CNN special, “The Imperial Presidency,” examines the history of US presidential power. From Truman to Trump, that power has been expanding—well beyond what the Founders intended—and we are now in unprecedented territory 

I’ll trace that history & share my own thoughts on what such powerful presidencies mean for American democracy. Tune in to watch
